family.description: Exploratory pilot of the BCH contextual conversion family: the established gf2 generator-matrix construction bch_generator_matrix_by_encoding (the rows of crates/gf2-coding/benches/bch_genmatrix.rs, B1 (15,5), B2 (127,64), B3 (255,223)) against the established M4RI construction of issue 4e732b56 (fill the k shifted copies of the generator polynomial, then mzd_echelonize_m4ri). Each timed call constructs a fresh k x n generator matrix from an already-constructed code (gf2 allocates a BitMatrix; M4RI copies the prefilled matrix through its cached allocator and reduces the copy); the two routes yield the same code in different systematic layouts, which the correctness gate checks by row-space equality. Code construction is setup outside the windows and is reported per execution. The baseline arm is always gf2 and the candidate is always M4RI, so a speedup above 1 means M4RI is ahead. These are current pinned measurements of both implementations, not a historical receipt and not an encoder throughput campaign; no cell here decides adoption.

effect.rationale: Comparator-gap cells only. This survey adopts no production implementation, so no worthwhile-speedup threshold applies and none is declared.
effect.equivalence_rationale: A 10% one-sided non-inferiority margin, provisional until this pilot measures the family's resolution; it is carried into the confirmatory addendum only if it strictly exceeds one plus the pilot-derived resolution. Pilot cells never yield a pass.
effect.material_gap_rationale: The arms use different algorithms (encode each basis vector versus reduce the shifted-polynomial matrix); a 20% whole-construction gap is the smallest difference worth attributing to a named cause (algorithmic operation count, allocation, word-level elimination) rather than to host noise; the pilot checks that it sits above the measured resolution before the confirmatory addendum freezes it.

complexity_budget.maintenance_rationale: The family reuses established harnesses and changes no production code; the whole diff is under dev/.
